newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK wants to clarify rules for future PLA garrison.
newsitem.headline: HK wants to clarify rules for future PLA garrison.

text.p: The Hong Kong government said on Monday it wanted clarification of the jurisdiction that Chinese military courts would have over a People's Liberation Army (PLA) garrison to be posted in the territory next year.
A Security Branch spokesman said the future legal framework governing the garrison in the territory would have to be familiar to Hong Kong people for it to be acceptable.
Hong Kong, a British colony for a century and a half, will revert to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997, and PLA troops will replace the British garrison.
"Greater clarity is needed in determining whether local courts or courts outside the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region should have jurisdiction," the spokesman said.
"At present, criminal cases to be tried in military courts are confined to very limited circumstances only," he said.

The statement followed China's recent announcement that offences committed by Chinese soldiers while on-duty would be tried by China's military court, while off-duty offences would be handled by local Hong Kong courts.
But the Hong Kong government said there were questions about offences committed against civilians, whether soldiers were on- or off-duty.
"Drink-driving whilst a soldier is on duty is a classic example. At present, such cases involving criminal charges will be dealt with by Hong Kong courts," the spokesman said.
The current practice was to hand over the case to civilian courts if the offence had injured a civilian, or if the offence had been committed with a civilian accomplice, he said.
